title: Geneva · Chamonix and Grand St Bernard Doorway
story: Alpine scenery with border-road discipline. This road trip is shaped as a ride, not as a shortcut: leave the start cleanly, use the first checkpoint for fuel and weather discipline, then ride Col des Montets with something in reserve. The best part sits around Col des Montets, Grand St Bernard approach, while Martigny fuel and Chamonix mountain town keep the day practical instead of turning it into a fuel hunt. Check the selected map before departure: scenic sections, transfer sections, speed/control reminders, risk points and the GPX checkpoint order are deliberately visible so the route is understandable before the engine starts. Ride it early if the area is popular, keep the photo stops legal, and shorten the route if weather, daylight or energy stops agreeing with the plan.

scenicChapters.title: Col des Montets
scenicChapters.narrative: 30 km that neither climbs nor drops much. The road settles into the ground rather than fighting it — this is where a day makes up time without anyone trying. Third and fourth, and very little else.
scenicChapters.riderNote: Check the pass is open before you commit to it.

scenicChapters.title: Great St Bernard Pass Road
scenicChapters.narrative: For 49 km this is Great St Bernard Pass Road, a road with a name of its own and a reason for it. Expect company on a summer weekend. Early is better than fast.

scenicChapters.title: Jura Crest Scenic Road
scenicChapters.narrative: Water arrives beside the road and stays for 44 km. The line follows the shore because there is nowhere else for it to go. Slow enough to look. The surface follows the shoreline, so the corners arrive where the water decided, not where an engineer did.
